sanskrit: rudhiraklinnagātras tu lakṣmaṇaḥ śubhalakṣaṇaḥ babhūva hṛṣṭas taṃ hatvā śakrajetāram āhave
english: Lakṣmaṇa, auspiciously marked, his limbs drenched with blood, became joyful having slain Śakrajit in battle.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa jāmbavantaṃ ca hanūmantaṃ ca vīryavān saṃnivartya mahātejās tāṃś ca sarvān vanaukasaḥ
english: Then that mighty hero of great splendour, having turned back Jāmbavān, Hanūmant, and all those forest-dwellers,

sanskrit: ājagāma tataḥ śīghraṃ yatra sugrīvarāghavau vibhīṣaṇam avaṣṭabhya hanūmantaṃ ca lakṣmaṇaḥ
english: came quickly to where Sugrīva and Rāghava were — Lakṣmaṇa, leaning on Vibhīṣaṇa and Hanūmant.

sanskrit: tato rāmam abhikramya saumitrir abhivādya ca tasthau bhrātṛsamīpasthaḥ śakrasyendrānujo yathā ācacakṣe tadā vīro ghoram indrajito vadham
english: Then Saumitri approached Rāma, saluted him, and stood near his brother as Indra's younger brother stands by Indra; and the hero then reported the terrible slaying of Indrajit.

sanskrit: rāvaṇas tu śiraś chinnaṃ lakṣmaṇena mahātmanā nyavedayata rāmāya tadā hṛṣṭo vibhīṣaṇaḥ
english: Vibhīṣaṇa, filled with joy, then reported to Rāma the severing of Rāvaṇa's son's head by the great-souled Lakṣmaṇa.

sanskrit: upaveśya tam utsaṅge pariṣvajyāvapīḍitam mūrdhni cainam upāghrāya bhūyaḥ saṃspṛśya ca tvaran uvāca lakṣmaṇaṃ vākyam āśvāsya puruṣarṣabhaḥ
english: That bull among men seated him on his lap, embraced him warmly, smelled his head, and touching him again and again in haste, spoke words to comfort Lakṣmaṇa.

sanskrit: kṛtaṃ paramakalyāṇaṃ karma duṣkarakāriṇā niramitraḥ kṛto 'smy adya niryāsyati hi rāvaṇaḥ balavyūhena mahatā śrutvā putraṃ nipātitam
english: "A most auspicious deed has been done by you, performer of the most difficult tasks. Today I am made free of enemies. For Rāvaṇa will march forth with a great arrayed force upon hearing that his son has been slain."

sanskrit: taṃ putravadhasaṃtaptaṃ niryāntaṃ rākṣasādhipam balenāvṛtya mahatā nihaniṣyāmi durjayam
english: "That lord of rākṣasas, scorched by the death of his son, when he sallies forth, I shall slay him — that unconquerable one — surrounding him with a great army."

sanskrit: tvayā lakṣmaṇa nāthena sītā ca pṛthivī ca me na duṣprāpā hate tv adya śakrajetari cāhave
english: "With you, Lakṣmaṇa, as my protector, neither Sītā nor the earth is beyond my reach — now that Śakrajit has been slain today in battle."

sanskrit: sa taṃ bhrātaram āśvāsya pāriṣvajya ca rāghavaḥ rāmaḥ suṣeṇaṃ muditaḥ samābhāṣyedam abravīt
english: Having consoled and embraced his brother, Rāghava Rāma, filled with delight, addressed Suṣeṇa and said this:

sanskrit: saśalyo 'yaṃ mahāprājñaḥ saumitrir mitravatsalaḥ yathā bhavati susvasthas tathā tvaṃ samupācara viśalyaḥ kriyatāṃ kṣipraṃ saumitriḥ savibhīṣaṇaḥ
english: "This great wise one, Saumitri, dear to his friends, still has arrows in him; treat him so that he fully recovers. Let Saumitri, together with Vibhīṣaṇa, be quickly freed of shafts."

sanskrit: kṛṣa vānarasainyānāṃ śūrāṇāṃ drumayodhinām ye cānye 'tra ca yudhyantaḥ saśalyā vraṇinas tathā te 'pi sarve prayatnena kriyantāṃ sukhinas tvayā
english: "Also tend to the brave monkey warriors, fighters from trees, and to all others here who fought and remain wounded with arrows — let all of them be carefully made comfortable by you."

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ sa rāmeṇa mahātmā hariyūthapaḥ lakṣmaṇāya dadau nastaḥ suṣeṇaḥ paramauṣadham
english: Thus addressed by Rāma, the great-souled Suṣeṇa, chief of the monkey troops, caused the supreme medicinal herb to be brought to the nose of Lakṣmaṇa.

sanskrit: sa tasya gandham āghrāya viśalyaḥ samapadyata tadā nirvedanaś caiva saṃrūḍhavraṇa eva ca
english: Having inhaled its fragrance, Lakṣmaṇa became free of all arrows at once, free of pain, and his wounds were healed.

sanskrit: vibhīṣaṇa mukhānāṃ ca suhṛdāṃ rāghavājñayā sarvavānaramukhyānāṃ cikitsāṃ sa tadākarot
english: Then by Rāghava's command, Suṣeṇa treated Vibhīṣaṇa and those allied friends, and all the foremost monkey leaders.

sanskrit: tataḥ prakṛtim āpanno hṛtaśalyo gatavyathaḥ saumitrir muditas tatra kṣaṇena vigatajvaraḥ
english: Then, free of arrows, free of pain, restored to his natural state, Saumitri, joyful, was in an instant rid of fever.

sanskrit: tathaiva rāmaḥ plavagādhipas tadā vibhīṣaṇaś carkṣapatiś ca jāmbavān avekṣya saumitrim arogam utthitaṃ mudā sasainyaḥ suciraṃ jaharṣire
english: Seeing Saumitri rise hale and healthy, Rāma, the king of the leaping monkeys, Vibhīṣaṇa, and Jāmbavān the lord of bears — along with their forces — rejoiced greatly and for a long time.

sanskrit: apūjayat karma sa lakṣmaṇasya suduṣkaraṃ dāśarathir mahātmā hṛṣṭā babhūvur yudhi yūthapendrā niśamya taṃ śakrajitaṃ nipātitam
english: The great-souled son of Daśaratha honoured Lakṣmaṇa's most extraordinary deed; and the chiefs of the monkey troops became exuberant upon hearing that Śakrajit had been brought down in battle.

sanskrit: tataḥ paulastya sacivāḥ śrutvā cendrajitaṃ hatam ācacakṣur abhijñāya daśagrīvāya savyathāḥ
english: Then the ministers of Paulastya, upon hearing that Indrajit was slain, and recognising the event, reported it with anguish to the ten-necked one.

sanskrit: yuddhe hato mahārāja lakṣmaṇena tavātmajaḥ vibhīṣaṇasahāyena miṣatāṃ no mahādyute
english: "O great king of great splendour, your son has been slain in battle by Lakṣmaṇa, aided by Vibhīṣaṇa, before our very eyes."

sanskrit: śūraḥ śūreṇa saṃgamya saṃyugeṣv aparājitaḥ lakṣṇanena hataḥ śūraḥ putras te vibudhendrajit
english: "Your heroic son, never defeated in battles, Vibudhendrajit — meeting hero against hero — has been slain by the hero Lakṣmaṇa."

sanskrit: sa taṃ pratibhayaṃ śrutvā vadhaṃ putrasya dāruṇam ghoram indrajitaḥ saṃkhye kaśmalaṃ prāviśan mahat
english: Hearing that terrifying, dreadful report of his son's cruel slaying — Indrajit's killing in battle — he fell into a great swoon.

sanskrit: upalabhya cirāt saṃjñāṃ rājā rākṣasapuṃgavaḥ putraśokārdito dīno vilalāpākulendriyaḥ
english: After a long time recovering his senses, the king, foremost among rākṣasas, tormented by grief for his son, wretched and his faculties overwhelmed, began to lament.

sanskrit: hā rākṣasacamūmukhya mama vatsa mahāratha jitvendraṃ katham adya tvaṃ lakṣmaṇasya vaśaṃ gataḥ
english: "Alas, O foremost of rākṣasa armies, my child, great chariot-warrior who had conquered Indra himself — how have you today come under the power of Lakṣmaṇa?"

sanskrit: nanu tvam iṣubhiḥ kruddho bhindyāḥ kālāntakāv api mandarasyāpi śṛṅgāṇi kiṃ punar lakṣmaṇaṃ raṇe
english: "Could you not, when enraged, pierce even Yama and Death with your arrows, could you not shatter even the peaks of mount Mandara — how then Lakṣmaṇa in battle?"

sanskrit: adya vaivasvato rājā bhūyo bahumato mama yenādya tvaṃ mahābāho saṃyuktaḥ kāladharmaṇā
english: "Today the king Vaivasvata is even more honoured by me — he by whom you, O mighty-armed one, have today been united with the law of time."

sanskrit: eṣa panthāḥ suyodhānāṃ sarvāmaragaṇeṣv api yaḥ kṛte hanyate bhartuḥ sa pumān svargam ṛcchati
english: "This is the path of great warriors even among all the hosts of immortals: the man who is slain for his master's sake attains heaven."

sanskrit: adya devagaṇāḥ sarve lokapālās tatharṣayaḥ hatam indrajitaṃ dṛṣṭvā sukhaṃ svapsyanti nirbhayāḥ
english: "Today all the hosts of gods, the world-guardians, and the sages will sleep in peace and without fear, having seen Indrajit slain."

sanskrit: adya lokās trayaḥ kṛtsnāḥ pṛthivī ca sakānanā ekenendrajitā hīnā śūṇyeva pratibhāti me
english: "Today the three entire worlds and the earth with all its forests, bereft of Indrajit alone, seem void to me."

sanskrit: adya nairṛtakanyāyāṃ śroṣyāmy antaḥpure ravam kareṇusaṃghasya yathā ninādaṃ girigahvare
english: "Today I shall hear in the inner apartments the wailing of the rākṣasa women, like the trumpeting of a herd of female elephants in a mountain cave."

sanskrit: yauvarājyaṃ ca laṅkāṃ ca rakṣāṃsi ca paraṃtapa mātaraṃ māṃ ca bhāryāṃ ca kva gato 'si vihāya naḥ
english: "O scorcher of foes, the crown-princeship, Laṅkā, the rākṣasas, your mother, me, and your wife — where have you gone, abandoning us all?"

sanskrit: mama nāma tvayā vīra gatasya yamasādanam pretakāryāṇi kāryāṇi viparīte hi vartase
english: "O hero, you who have gone to the abode of Yama — the funeral rites must be performed in your name; yet you conduct yourself in the inverse order, for you have preceded me."

sanskrit: sa tvaṃ jīvati sugrīve rāghave ca salakṣmaṇe mama śalyam anuddhṛtya kva gato 'si vihāya naḥ
english: "While Sugrīva still lives, and Rāghava with Lakṣmaṇa, you have gone without removing the thorn from my heart — where have you gone, leaving us?"

sanskrit: evamādivilāpārtaṃ rāvaṇaṃ rākṣasādhipam āviveśa mahān kopaḥ putravyasanasaṃbhavaḥ
english: Rāvaṇa, the lord of rākṣasas, afflicted with laments such as these, was then seized by a great rage born of the calamity of his son's death.

sanskrit: ghoraṃ prakṛtyā rūpaṃ tat tasya krodhāgnimūrchitam babhūva rūpaṃ rudrasya kruddhasyeva durāsadam
english: His form, dreadful by nature, now blazing and swollen with the fire of rage, became like the form of Rudra when wrathful — unapproachable.

sanskrit: tasya kruddhasya netrābhyāṃ prāpatann asrabindavaḥ dīptābhyām iva dīpābhyāṃ sārciṣaḥ snehabindavaḥ
english: From his enraged eyes, drops of tears fell — like drops of oil with flames from two burning lamps.

sanskrit: dantān vidaśatas tasya śrūyate daśanasvanaḥ yantrasyāveṣṭyamānasya mahato dānavair iva
english: As he gnashed his teeth, the sound of his grinding was heard like that of a great machine being turned by dānavas.

sanskrit: kālāgnir iva saṃkruddho yāṃ yāṃ diśam avaikṣata tasyāṃ tasyāṃ bhayatrastā rākṣasāḥ saṃnililyire
english: Like the fire of Time when fully enraged, into whichever direction he looked, the rākṣasas there, terrified, crouched and hid themselves.

sanskrit: tam antakam iva kruddhaṃ carācaracikhādiṣum vīkṣamāṇaṃ diśaḥ sarvā rākṣasā nopacakramuḥ
english: Like Death himself when wrathful, desirous of devouring the moving and stationary, as he gazed in all directions, no rākṣasa dared approach him.

sanskrit: tataḥ paramasaṃkruddho rāvaṇo rākṣasādhipaḥ abravīd rakṣasāṃ madhye saṃstambhayiṣur āhave
english: Then Rāvaṇa, supremely enraged, the lord of rākṣasas, spoke in the midst of the rākṣasas, wishing to rally them for battle:

sanskrit: mayā varṣasahasrāṇi caritvā duścaraṃ tapaḥ teṣu teṣv avakāśeṣu svayambhūḥ paritoṣitaḥ
english: "Having performed for thousands of years the most difficult austerities in diverse retreats, I satisfied the Self-Born one."

sanskrit: tasyaiva tapaso vyuṣṭyā prasādāc ca svayambhuvaḥ nāsurebhyo na devebhyo bhayaṃ mama kadā cana
english: "By the fruit of that very austerity and by the grace of the Self-Born, I have never had fear from asuras or from gods."

sanskrit: kavacaṃ brahmadattaṃ me yad ādityasamaprabham devāsuravimardeṣu na bhinnaṃ vajraśaktibhiḥ
english: "The armour given me by Brahmā, equal in brilliance to the sun, has not been pierced in the conflicts of gods and asuras even by the vajra or the śakti-spear."

sanskrit: tena mām adya saṃyuktaṃ rathastham iha saṃyuge pratīyāt ko 'dya mām ājau sākṣād api puraṃdaraḥ
english: "Who today, equipped with that armour and standing on my chariot in this fight, shall face me in battle — even Purandara himself?"

sanskrit: yat tadābhiprasannena saśaraṃ kārmukaṃ mahat devāsuravimardeṣu mama dattaṃ svayambhuvā
english: "That great bow along with arrows, given to me by the propitious Self-Born one for use in conflicts of gods and asuras —"

sanskrit: adya tūryaśatair bhīmaṃ dhanur utthāpyatāṃ mahat rāmalakṣmaṇayor eva vadhāya paramāhave
english: "— let that great and formidable bow be brought forward today with hundreds of drums sounding, for the slaying of Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa in the supreme battle."

sanskrit: sa putravadhasaṃtaptaḥ śūraḥ krodhavaśaṃ gataḥ samīkṣya rāvaṇo buddhyā sītāṃ hantuṃ vyavasyata
english: That hero, scorched by the death of his son and overcome by rage, Rāvaṇa, after deliberating in his mind, resolved to kill Sītā.

sanskrit: pratyavekṣya tu tāmrākṣaḥ sughoro ghoradarśanān dīno dīnasvarān sarvāṃs tān uvāca niśācarān
english: With his copper-red eyes, he looked around and, terrible-visaged, wretched, with a wretched voice, he addressed all those night-wanderers:

sanskrit: māyayā mama vatsena vañcanārthaṃ vanaukasām kiṃ cid eva hataṃ tatra sīteyam iti darśitam
english: "Through my son's illusion, in order to deceive the forest-dwellers, a semblance of slaughter was shown there, and Sītā was shown as if dead."

sanskrit: tad idaṃ satyam evāhaṃ kariṣye priyam ātmanaḥ vaidehīṃ nāśayiṣyāmi kṣatrabandhum anuvratām ity evam uktvā sacivān khaḍgam āśu parāmṛśat
english: "Now I shall truly do what pleases me — I shall destroy Vaidehī, who faithfully follows that base kṣatriya." Having said this to his counsellors, he quickly seized his sword.

sanskrit: uddhṛtya guṇasaṃpannaṃ vimalāmbaravarcasaṃ niṣpapāta sa vegena sabhāyāḥ sacivair vṛtaḥ
english: Drawing it — that sword full of virtues, as bright as the clear sky — he rushed forth swiftly from the assembly hall, surrounded by his counsellors.

sanskrit: rāvaṇaḥ putraśokena bhṛśam ākulacetanaḥ saṃkruddhaḥ khaḍgam ādāya sahasā yatra maithilī
english: Rāvaṇa, his mind greatly agitated by grief for his son, enraged, taking up his sword, rushed to where Maithilī was.

sanskrit: vrajantaṃ rākṣasaṃ prekṣya siṃhanādaṃ pracukruśuḥ ūcuś cānyonyam āśliṣya saṃkruddhaṃ prekṣya rākṣasāḥ
english: Seeing the rākṣasa striding forward, the rākṣasas roared a lion-roar and, embracing one another, spoke to each other, beholding him in his fury:

sanskrit: adyainaṃ tāv ubhau dṛṣṭvā bhrātarau pravyathiṣyataḥ lokapālā hi catvāraḥ kruddhenānena nirjitāḥ bahavaḥ śatravaś cānye saṃyugeṣv abhipātitāḥ
english: "Today those two brothers, seeing him, will be distressed. For the four world-guardians were conquered by this one in his fury, and many other enemies were laid low by him in battles."

sanskrit: teṣāṃ saṃjalpamānānām aśokavanikāṃ gatām abhidudrāva vaidehīṃ rāvaṇaḥ krodhamūrchitaḥ
english: While they were thus talking amongst themselves, Rāvaṇa, intoxicated with rage, rushed toward Vaidehī who was in the aśoka grove.

sanskrit: vāryamāṇaḥ susaṃkruddhaḥ suhṛdbhir hitabuddhibhiḥ abhyadhāvata saṃkruddhaḥ khe graho rohiṇīm iva
english: Though restrained by friends of good intent, he charged forward, fully enraged, like a planet seizing Rohiṇī in the sky.

sanskrit: maithilī rakṣyamāṇā tu rākṣasībhir aninditā dadarśa rākṣasaṃ kruddhaṃ nistriṃśavaradhāriṇam
english: Maithilī, the blameless one, who was being guarded by the rākṣasī women, then saw the rākṣasa, wrathful and bearing a fine sword.

sanskrit: taṃ niśāmya sanistriṃśaṃ vyathitā janakātmajā nivāryamāṇaṃ bahuśaḥ suhṛdbhir anivartinam
english: Beholding him sword in hand, the daughter of Janaka was overcome with distress, seeing him who, though restrained many times by friends, would not turn back.

sanskrit: yathāyaṃ mām abhikruddhaḥ samabhidravati svayam vadhiṣyati sanāthāṃ mām anāthām iva durmatiḥ
english: "As this one charges toward me himself, enraged, the evil-minded one will slay me — who has a protector — as if I were without one."

sanskrit: bahuśaś codayām āsa bhartāraṃ mām anuvratām bhāryā bhava ramasyeti pratyākhyāto 'bhavan mayā
english: "He urged me many times: 'Be the wife of Rāvaṇa,' urging me who am devoted to my husband — but he was refused by me."

sanskrit: so 'yaṃ mām anupasthānād vyaktaṃ nairāśyam āgataḥ krodhamohasamāviṣṭo nihantuṃ māṃ samudyataḥ
english: "This one, having clearly reached despair at my non-compliance, is now seized by rage and delusion, and is prepared to kill me."

sanskrit: atha vā tau naravyāghrau bhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau mannimittam anāryeṇa samare 'dya nipātitau aho dhin mannimitto 'yaṃ vināśo rājaputrayoḥ
english: "Or perhaps those two tiger-like men, the brothers Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, have been struck down today in battle by this ignoble one on account of me. Alas, shame — this destruction of the two princes is on account of me!"

sanskrit: hanūmato hi tadvākyaṃ na kṛtaṃ kṣudrayā mayā yady ahaṃ tasya pṛṣṭhena tadāyāsam aninditā nādyaivam anuśoceyaṃ bhartur aṅkagatā satī
english: "That word of Hanūmant was not heeded by me in my wretchedness. Had I, blameless one, come then upon his back, I would not be lamenting thus today, seated in my husband's lap as a faithful wife."

sanskrit: manye tu hṛdayaṃ tasyāḥ kausalyāyāḥ phaliṣyati ekaputrā yadā putraṃ vinaṣṭaṃ śroṣyate yudhi
english: "I think the heart of Kausalyā will be fulfilled — when she, who has but one son, hears that her son has perished in battle."

sanskrit: sā hi janma ca bālyaṃ ca yauvanaṃ ca mahātmanaḥ dharmakāryāṇi rūpaṃ ca rudatī saṃsramiṣyati
english: "She, weeping, will recall the birth, childhood, and youth of that great-souled one, and his acts of righteousness and his beauty."

sanskrit: nirāśā nihate putre dattvā śrāddham acetanā agnim ārokṣyate nūnam apo vāpi pravekṣyati
english: "Without hope, her son slain, having performed the śrāddha rite, senseless, she will surely mount the funeral pyre or enter the waters."

sanskrit: dhig astu kubjām asatīṃ mantharāṃ pāpaniścayām yannimittam idaṃ duḥkhaṃ kausalyā pratipatsyate
english: "Shame upon the hunchback, the wicked Mantharā of evil resolve — because of whom Kausalyā will obtain this sorrow."

sanskrit: ity evaṃ maithilīṃ dṛṣṭvā vilapantīṃ tapasvinīm rohiṇīm iva candreṇa vinā grahavaśaṃ gatām
english: Thus seeing Maithilī, the wretched one, lamenting — like Rohiṇī separated from the moon and seized by a planet —

sanskrit: supārśvo nāma medhāvī rāvaṇaṃ rākṣaseśvaram nivāryamāṇaṃ sacivair idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: — the wise one named Supārśva spoke these words to Rāvaṇa, the lord of rākṣasas, as he was being restrained by the counsellors:

sanskrit: kathaṃ nāma daśagrīva sākṣād vaiśravaṇānuja hantum icchasi vaidehīṃ krodhād dharmam apāsya hi
english: "How is it, O ten-necked one, O own brother of Vaiśravaṇa, that you wish to slay Vaidehī, casting aside dharma in your rage?"

sanskrit: veda vidyāvrata snātaḥ svadharmanirataḥ sadā striyāḥ kasmād vadhaṃ vīra manyase rākṣaseśvara
english: "O hero, lord of rākṣasas, you who are versed in the Vedas, who have completed your studies and vows, who are always devoted to your own dharma — why do you contemplate the slaying of a woman?"

sanskrit: maithilīṃ rūpasaṃpannāṃ pratyavekṣasva pārthiva tvam eva tu sahāsmābhī rāghave krodham utsṛja
english: "Behold Maithilī endowed with beauty, O king. Together with us, direct your anger at Rāghava himself."

sanskrit: abhyutthānaṃ tvam adyaiva kṛṣṇapakṣacaturdaśīm kṛtvā niryāhy amāvāsyāṃ vijayāya balair vṛtaḥ
english: "Making preparations today on the fourteenth of the dark fortnight, go forth on the new-moon day, surrounded by your forces, for victory."

sanskrit: śūro dhīmān rathī khaḍgī rathapravaram āsthitaḥ hatvā dāśarathiṃ rāmaṃ bhavān prāpsyati maithilīm
english: "You, a hero, wise, a chariot-warrior, sword-bearer, mounting the finest chariot — having slain Rāma the son of Daśaratha, you shall obtain Maithilī."

sanskrit: sa tad durātmā suhṛdā niveditaṃ vacaḥ sudharmyaṃ pratigṛhya rāvaṇaḥ gṛhaṃ jagāmātha tataś ca vīryavān punaḥ sabhāṃ ca prayayau suhṛdvṛtaḥ
english: That wicked-souled Rāvaṇa accepted the righteous words communicated by his friend, and went home; then that mighty one again proceeded to the assembly hall, accompanied by his friends.

sanskrit: sa praviśya sabhāṃ rājā dīnaḥ paramaduḥkhitaḥ niṣasādāsane mukhye siṃhaḥ kruddha iva śvasan
english: Entering the assembly hall, the king, wretched and deeply grieved, sat down in the foremost seat, breathing like an angry lion.

sanskrit: abravīc ca tadā sarvān balamukhyān mahābalaḥ rāvaṇaḥ prāñjalīn vākyaṃ putravyasanakarśitaḥ
english: Then mighty Rāvaṇa, wasted by the calamity of his son's death, addressed all the chiefs of the army with joined palms, and spoke:

sanskrit: sarve bhavantaḥ sarveṇa hastyaśvena samāvṛtāḥ niryāntu rathasaṃghaiś ca pādātaiś copaśobhitāḥ
english: "Let all of you, accompanied by all the elephants and horses, go forth, adorned with hosts of chariots and infantry."

sanskrit: ekaṃ rāmaṃ parikṣipya samare hantum arhatha prahṛṣṭā śaravarṣeṇa prāvṛṭkāla ivāmbudāḥ
english: "Surrounding Rāma alone in battle, you ought to slay him, rejoicing, with a downpour of arrows — like rain clouds at the onset of the monsoon season."

sanskrit: atha vāhaṃ śarais tīkṣṇair bhinnagātraṃ mahāraṇe bhavadbhiḥ śvo nihantāsmi rāmaṃ lokasya paśyataḥ
english: "Or else I myself, tomorrow in the great battle, with sharp arrows, his body pierced by you, shall slay Rāma before the eyes of the world."

sanskrit: ity evaṃ rākṣasendrasya vākyam ādāya rākṣasāḥ niryayus te rathaiḥ śīghraṃ nāgānīkaiś ca saṃvṛtāḥ
english: Taking these words of the lord of rākṣasas to heart, the rākṣasas marched forth swiftly in chariots, surrounded by elephant formations.

sanskrit: sa saṃgrāmo mahābhīmaḥ sūryasyodayanaṃ prati rakṣasāṃ vānarāṇāṃ ca tumulaḥ samapadyata
english: At sunrise, a most fearsome and tumultuous battle between the rākṣasas and the monkeys took place.

sanskrit: te gadābhir vicitrābhiḥ prāsaiḥ khaḍgaiḥ paraśvadhaiḥ anyonyaṃ samare jaghnus tadā vānararākṣasāḥ
english: The monkeys and rākṣasas struck one another in battle with variegated maces, lances, swords, and battle-axes.

sanskrit: mātaṃgarathakūlasya vājimatsyā dhvajadrumāḥ śarīrasaṃghāṭavahāḥ prasasruḥ śoṇitāpagāḥ
english: Rivers of blood flowed, carrying the flotsam of that massed host of elephants and chariots — with horses as fish, banners as trees, and heaps of bodies as their current.

sanskrit: dhvajavarmarathān aśvān nānāpraharaṇāni ca āplutyāplutya samare vānarendrā babhañjire
english: The monkey chieftains, leaping and leaping again in battle, shattered banners, armour, chariots, horses, and various weapons.

sanskrit: keśān karṇalalāṭāṃś ca nāsikāś ca plavaṃgamāḥ rakṣasāṃ daśanais tīkṣṇaiḥ nakhaiś cāpi vyakartayan
english: The leaping monkeys tore apart the hair, ears, foreheads, and noses of the rākṣasas with their sharp teeth and nails.

sanskrit: ekaikaṃ rākṣasaṃ saṃkhye śataṃ vānarapuṃgavāḥ abhyadhāvanta phalinaṃ vṛkṣaṃ śakunayo yathā
english: In battle, a hundred foremost monkeys rushed upon each single rākṣasa, as birds rush upon a fruit-laden tree.

sanskrit: tathā gadābhir gurvībhiḥ prāsaiḥ khaḍgaiḥ paraśvadhaiḥ nirjaghnur vānarān ghorān rākṣasāḥ parvatopamāḥ
english: Similarly, the rākṣasas, mountain-like, slaughtered the fierce monkeys with heavy maces, lances, swords, and battle-axes.

sanskrit: rākṣasair vadhyamānānāṃ vānarāṇāṃ mahācamūḥ śaraṇyaṃ śaraṇaṃ yātā rāmaṃ daśarathātmajam
english: The great army of monkeys, being slaughtered by the rākṣasas, sought refuge in Rāma the son of Daśaratha, who is worthy of refuge.

sanskrit: tato rāmo mahātejā dhanur ādāya vīryavān praviśya rākṣasaṃ sainyaṃ śaravarṣaṃ vavarṣa ha
english: Then Rāma of great splendour, mighty, taking up his bow, entered the rākṣasa army and rained down a torrent of arrows.

sanskrit: praviṣṭaṃ tu tadā rāmaṃ meghāḥ sūryam ivāmbare nābhijagmur mahāghoraṃ nirdahantaṃ śarāgninā
english: But they could not approach Rāma as he entered — most dreadful, burning them with the fire of his arrows — just as clouds do not approach the sun in the sky.

sanskrit: kṛtāny eva sughorāṇi rāmeṇa rajanīcarāḥ raṇe rāmasya dadṛśuḥ karmāṇy asukarāṇi ca
english: The night-wanderers witnessed in battle the most dreadful deeds already wrought by Rāma, and his extraordinary feats.

sanskrit: cālayantaṃ mahānīkaṃ vidhamantaṃ mahārathān dadṛśus te na vai rāmaṃ vātaṃ vanagataṃ yathā
english: They saw him shaking the great host, scattering the great warriors — yet they did not truly see Rāma, just as one does not see wind that has entered a forest.

sanskrit: chinnaṃ bhinnaṃ śarair dagdhaṃ prabhagnaṃ śastrapīḍitam balaṃ rāmeṇa dadṛśur na ramaṃ śīghrakāriṇam
english: They saw the army cut down, split apart, burned by arrows, shattered, afflicted by weapons — but they did not see Rāma, the swift in action.

sanskrit: praharantaṃ śarīreṣu na te paśyanti rāghavam indriyārtheṣu tiṣṭhantaṃ bhūtātmānam iva prajāḥ
english: Striking at their bodies, they did not perceive Rāghava — just as living beings do not perceive the soul of all existence dwelling in the objects of the senses.

sanskrit: eṣa hanti gajānīkam eṣa hanti mahārathān eṣa hanti śarais tīkṣṇaiḥ padātīn vājibhiḥ saha
english: "Here he slays the elephant formations, here he slays the great chariot-warriors, here he slays the infantry and cavalry together with sharp arrows!"

sanskrit: iti te rākṣasāḥ sarve rāmasya sadṛśān raṇe anyonyakupitā jaghnuḥ sādṛśyād rāghavasya te
english: Thus all those rākṣasas, enraged with one another in battle, struck those who looked like Rāma — owing to their resemblance to Rāghava.

sanskrit: na te dadṛśire rāmaṃ dahantam arivāhinīm mohitāḥ paramāstreṇa gāndharveṇa mahātmanā
english: They did not see Rāma burning the enemy host, confused by the supreme Gāndharva weapon of that great-souled one.

sanskrit: te tu rāmasahasrāṇi raṇe paśyanti rākṣasāḥ punaḥ paśyanti kākutstham ekam eva mahāhave
english: The rākṣasas in battle saw thousands of Rāmas; then again in the great combat they saw only one Kākutstha.

sanskrit: bhramantīṃ kāñcanīṃ koṭiṃ kārmukasya mahātmanaḥ alātacakrapratimāṃ dadṛśus te na rāghavam
english: They saw the whirling golden tip of that great-souled one's bow, resembling a revolving firebrand wheel — but they did not see Rāghava.

sanskrit: śarīranābhi sattvārciḥ śarīraṃ nemikārmukam jyāghoṣatalanirghoṣaṃ tejobuddhiguṇaprabham
english: His body was the hub, the flame of his valour was the spokes, his body with bow was the rim, the sound of his bowstring and the clapping of his palm were its noise, brilliant with the qualities of his energy and intelligence —

sanskrit: divyāstraguṇaparyantaṃ nighnantaṃ yudhi rākṣasān dadṛśū rāmacakraṃ tat kālacakram iva prajāḥ
english: — bounded at its edge by the qualities of divine weapons, that wheel of Rāma slaying rākṣasas in battle was seen by the people like the wheel of Time itself.

sanskrit: anīkaṃ daśasāhasraṃ rathānāṃ vātaraṃhasām aṣṭādaśasahasrāṇi kuñjarāṇāṃ tarasvinām
english: A force of ten thousand swift-as-wind chariots, eighteen thousand swift elephants,

sanskrit: caturdaśasahasrāṇi sārohāṇāṃ ca vājinām pūrṇe śatasahasre dve rākṣasānāṃ padātinām
english: fourteen thousand horsemen together with their riders, and a full two hundred thousand rākṣasa foot-soldiers —

sanskrit: divasasyāṣṭame bhāge śarair agniśikhopamaiḥ hatāny ekena rāmeṇa rakṣasāṃ kāmarūpiṇām
english: — all of these shape-shifting rākṣasas were slain, in one eighth part of the day, by Rāma alone with arrows resembling tongues of flame.

sanskrit: te hatāśvā hatarathāḥ śrāntā vimathitadhvajāḥ abhipetuḥ purīṃ laṅkāṃ hataśeṣā niśācarāḥ
english: Those night-wanderers who remained alive, their horses slain, their chariots destroyed, exhausted, their banners scattered, fled back to the city of Laṅkā.

sanskrit: hatair gajapadāty aśvais tad babhūva raṇājiram ākrīḍabhūmī rudrasya kruddhasyeva pinākinaḥ
english: Strewn with slain elephants, infantry, and horses, that battle-ground became like the playground of Rudra the wielder of the Pināka bow, when wrathful.

sanskrit: tato devāḥ sagandharvāḥ siddhāś ca paramarṣayaḥ sādhu sādhv iti rāmasya tat karma samapūjayan
english: Then the gods together with the gandharvas, the siddhas, and the supreme sages honoured Rāma's deed with cries of "Well done! Well done!"

sanskrit: abravīc ca tadā rāmaḥ sugrīvaṃ pratyanantaram etad astrabalaṃ divyaṃ mama vā tryambakasya vā
english: And Rāma then said in reply to Sugrīva: "This power of divine weapons belongs to me or to Tryambaka — the Three-eyed one."

sanskrit: nihatya tāṃ rākṣasavāhinīṃ tu rāmas tadā śakrasamo mahātmā astreṣu śastreṣu jitaklamaś ca saṃstūyate devagaṇaiḥ prahṛṣṭaiḥ
english: Having slain that rākṣasa host, Rāma — the great-souled one, equal to Śakra, triumphant in weapons and arms, his weariness overcome — was then praised by the exultant hosts of gods.
